phase: PRECOMMITTED BEFORE READING languageCapability.matrix values, fixture valid fields, checker source, or conformance expected results
method: Read the normalization-level definitions and language safety rules, then independently judged the four language rows. Fixture outcomes were derived from their human rationale and input fields only.

languageCapability.reason: The scanner can preserve token boundaries and semantic binding analysis can rename locals; triple-slash, ts-check/ignore, source-map and JSDoc-like comment semantics make comment removal require a preserved-directive subset.

Token-aware lexical normalization is available. Doc comments lower to attributes and macro token trees complicate comment and local-binding normalization; deep semantics can handle ordinary locals but source macros prevent an unconditional full claim.

Indentation/newline layout is semantic, and encoding/type/noqa-style comments require preservation. Under the stated product tier, no complete semantic binding substrate is promised for safe local-only renaming.

Whitespace participates in semicolon insertion, and build/line/go directives are comment-shaped. The product does not promise Go as one of its two deep semantic languages, so safe binding-aware renaming is unavailable in this architecture.

transitionFixtureOutcomes.condition: A witness must relate old and new occurrence groups without pretending one-to-one identity.

knownLimitations: This is an architecture/toolchain judgment, not a compiled golden corpus. Macro expansion, generated code, JSX, and language-version edges can lower a capability.
The level fixture IDs themselves encode some intended outcomes; the independent value lies mainly in the language matrix and transition semantics.
No existing implementation shape was used as a merit argument; the product's stated deep-language boundary was treated as a design input.
